title: Finite-support Weyl cylinder form invariance and weighted square-root products
question: Does the finite Q3 Friedrichs form domain remain invariant under finite-support Weyl multipliers, with explicit two-orientation weighted square-root product bounds?

model.weyl_multiplier: A_t(q)=exp(i sum_j t_j q_j) on a finite-support cylinder, with |A_t|=1 and |grad A_t|^2=||t||_2^2
model.shifted_forms: K_on and K_edge are the closed positive Friedrichs forms from EXP-001131, with common form domain and K_edge <= 21 K_on
model.product_rule: For either shifted form q_K, q_K[A_t psi] <= 2 q_K[psi] + ||t||_2^2/chi ||psi||^2 on the common core, hence A_t preserves the form domain
model.weighted_bound: ||K_K^(1/2) A_t K_K^(-1/2)||^2 <= 2+||t||_2^2/chi; cross-orientation products have squared bound at most 21(2+||t||_2^2/chi)

adversarial_review.check: A_t is a modulus-one multiplication operator, so the potential and bond terms are unchanged; only the kinetic product rule contributes.
The bound uses the exact squared gradient norm ||t||_2^2/chi and the safe inequality |a+b|^2<=2|a|^2+2|b|^2; no missing factor of two is hidden.
The product is defined through the closed form and K^{-1/2}; this does not assert a bounded commutator or an operator-domain identity for arbitrary unbounded observables.
Same-form and cross-orientation products are separated; the cross bound pays the exact degree-six multiplier 21 from EXP-001131.
For a fixed finite support vector t, the constant is independent of volume within the degree-six graph class, but no thermodynamic dynamics or common alpha follows.
The Weyl cylinder algebra is only a bounded test algebra; modular transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks exact rational squared-gradient, support-norm and cross-orientation constants; it does not formalize multiplication operators, form representation, or QFT limits.

qft_interface.closed: Finite-support Weyl cylinder multipliers preserve both finite-volume shifted form domains and have explicit same- and cross-orientation weighted square-root bounds uniform in volume for bounded-degree graphs.
qft_interface.open: All bounded local observables, unbounded polynomial products, modular/cutoff/beta transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum and Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: This is a bounded Weyl-cylinder bridge toward the QFT algebra; it supplies no heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner.

no_overclaim: This closes only the declared finite-support Weyl-cylinder form-invariance and weighted-product estimate. It is not an arbitrary-observable domain theorem, a modular dynamics result, a common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A result.
